previous_model_claim: 376 and 375 establish two distinct Booty judgments
assessment: previous error label not supported; native pinpoint and parallel report corroborate a printed typo in the citing judgment
reason: Drover prints Booty v Hutton 2009 BCCA 376 at para26 and 275 BCAC139; native Booty 2009 BCCA375 para26 states exactly the rebuttable presumption cited by Drover. Different printed numbers alone do not establish two genuine judgments. The historical review label is preserved; this supplemental adjudication disputes it. No forced split is introduced merely to clear an old model label.

sources.label: target_pinpoint
sources.text: [26] Ms. Booty has not put forward any particulars of prejudice she has suffered as a result of the delay, but as Madam Justice Saunders commented in Greither v. Greither, 2005 BCCA 339 at para. 20, there is always some prejudice in a delay in pursuing an appeal. Where the delay is inordinate and inexcusable, a rebuttable presumption of prejudice arises: see Busse v. Robinson Morelli Chertkow, 1999 BCCA 313, [1999] 10 W.W.R. 692 at para. 18. In the case at bar, the presumption of prejudice has not been rebutted.

sources.text: [71] As there has been inordinate and inexcusable delay, a rebuttable presumption of prejudice arises: Booty v. Hutton, 2009 BCCA 376 at para. 26, 275 B.C.A.C. 139. That presumption includes the fact that the respondents have been denied the orderly conduct of the Service Appeal: Versluce Estate v. Knol, 2008 YKCA 18 at para. 8, 263 B.C.A.C. 65, leave to appeal ref'd [2009] 1 S.C.R. x.
